items.title: 52035_Eddie Durham oral history interview
items.q: I said, oh, Macio, I'll go right over there

ctx.x: And he had a band up in Hartford and they said he was the king of the saxophone up there.

And clarinet. That's right, nobody could challenge him on that tenor. And the clarinet. I said, oh, Macio, I'll go right over there, so about three days later I went to Hartford and got him. And I said, where's your baritone -- he played them all -- somebody said, oh, he put that in pawn. Where's his tenor. He pawned that too. Where, he ain't got no ticket.

And he was sick from that drinking, I brought him to Newark by my sister, where she was living and mother and we wouldn't let him do anything. We kept him there and finally put him -- doctor and got him in the hospital and he got all right. Stayed all right for quite awhile.
